title: Ophanim · Opening drive dialogue
notes: Generated from src/data/opening-prologue.js by scripts/export-runtime-narrative.mjs. Read-only: the game reads the module, not this document. Edit the module (or move the dialogue into content/narrative) and relaunch the studio.

lines.text: You have been driving for a long time. It is raining on the road. The wipers go.
You blink.
It is a long blink.
Your thumb is resting on the seam of the steering wheel. You can feel the join in the leather.
There you are.
It is a voice, and it is not in the van. It arrives the way a room arrives when the fridge cuts out.
I kept your place.
Who is that?
Nobody you would have on the form. I keep late hours. I have been the cough in a slow movement, and the string that goes in the last eight bars.
I have been the chair that creaks on the only good take. I am very well thought of. Nobody has ever once asked me to leave.
I'm driving.
You are! Beautifully. Both hands. This will not take a moment. It never takes a moment; that is what I like about it.
The wipers have not come back across. You notice that they have not come back across.
You say nothing. You are good at it. It is on your invoice.
Good. Do not start talking now. You would only have to stop again at the door.
Three wheels have torn away from one another and gone on turning, round a hole in nothing. The wheels are full of eyes.
Before the job. Shall we see what you can keep still?

choices.text: "I'm keeping my hands on the wheel."

lines.text: Your hands have not moved. The eyes have.
Still here. You may ask another, or we can get on with the job.
No. I am not doing a test for you.
Of course not. Keep your hands where you want them. I will keep mine.
One eye shuts. The wheels go on turning.
There. That is an answer too.
What am I looking at?
I do not think I am on your side of that question.
You count twenty-four eyes. Twenty-three close. The last seems nearer than the wheel that carries it.
There. One each. I will not look away if you do not.
You first.
Oh, I can.
The last eye goes dark. You still feel watched from exactly there.
Now what were you going to do about the job?
For a moment there is no room to look beside it. Your own eye begins to water.
You can hold a look. Good. A minute is longer than that.
I'm keeping my hands on the wheel.
You can still feel the seam under your thumb. The thumb is steady. The seam makes one complete turn.
Keep the hands. They are yours. The position is the doubtful part.
Three eyes close, one after another. The seam stops moving. You have not moved your hands.
That will do. You can keep a position. They will like that about you.
You spread your fingers. The seam stays against your thumb anyway.
Excellent. You are not doing it, then.
You turn from the wheels. The dark is exactly as deep on this side.
Better? I can wait. The road cannot.
You wait for something to arrive at the edge of your sight. Nothing does.
You are remarkably good at this. Are you sure this is your first night?
The wheels are where you left them. You have the unpleasant thought that you have come back on a different side.
You give it no answer. The eyes shut in order, as though a name is being read against each one.
No. That was not empty. You were waiting for me to fill it.
You stop waiting. You cannot tell whether that is different.
Keep that one. You may need it in a room.
The wheels go on turning. One eye has stayed shut. It does not open when you stop looking.
There. You have changed the view. You can do that. The job will require rather more of you.
Ask me about the job.
Tell me about the job. Go on. I love how people tell it.

choices.text: "Five rooms. A clean minute of each."

lines.text: Five rooms. A clean minute of each.
With nothing in it.
With nothing in it. A studio, the pool, the concert hall, the practice wing and the chapel.
Four hundred quid.
To stand very still in five rooms and not be there. I have known people do it for nothing. I have known people do it for years.
It's just a job.
It is a lovely job. They ring a man who does not ask, and he does not ask. That is why they have your number.
The sheet is on the passenger seat. Ellery Conservatoire of Music, condemned. Demolition begins 06:00 Thursday. Bring a light.
One clean minute of each, with nothing in it. No handling noise, no clothing, no breath.
No breath! Read me the next bit. I could hear it all night. I do.
If you can hear yourself on the take, the take is not the room, and we will not accept it.
Who wants a minute of an empty room, do you suppose?
Who signed for W. Ellery Holdings?
A good question.
The signature is illegible. The authorising officer's field is blank under every carbon.
There. Now you have asked, and it cost you nothing. It is a very old firm.
I don't ask.
No. Neither did the last one.
The prior contractor delivered four accepted room tones. The packet was settled for four. The account remains open.
What happened to the fifth?
It is still undelivered. It is a very patient invoice. "When five clean minutes are received, the account is satisfied." That is the one sentence on the sheet I would call sincere.
What happened to him?
He is nearly finished. Ask him. He has been nearly finished for some time.
Not my problem.
No. It is your job. There is a difference, and you have about eight hours to find out what it is.
You have not asked what it was. They never do. Have a look.
There is a below, it turns out. Wet tarmac, railings, a tree somebody planted on purpose. A long front with its power off.
Public baths, to begin with. 1912, blue tile, people went in to get clean. Then a school bought the baths, and the pub, and half the street.
It never stopped being about getting clean.
There is more on the file. You can ask, or leave it there.

choices.text: "What does that leave me to hear?"

lines.text: What else?
What does that leave me to hear?
By midnight you will be standing in those rooms, being paid to hear nothing. Somebody ought to tell you what you will be hearing nothing of.
You say nothing. The notice has not been answered. Your work order has.
Five clean minutes. You see the difficulty.
What kind of school?
Did you go there?
I attended. Every lesson, every night, every year, the best seat in the house. You will not find me on a register. I have looked.
You keep quiet. It tells you anyway.
They take a child who can hear, and correct it. Reference listening. The same bar, the same small fault. Again. Again.
Until you can hear a wrong note through a wall, in your sleep, in your mother saying your name.
You have worked with people who came out of Ellery. They flinch at fridges.
One got very good. He could hear everything. Then he stopped coming down to lessons.
The boy was recovered from a chamber room upstairs. The public register still calls him missing.
Recovery entered on the internal sheet. External register to retain MISSING. Medical finding: not attached.
The others knew. They would not play over it.
What was his name?
Now that is a question. Nobody asks it. It is the only thing in that building still correctly filed, and you will not get it from me.
What happened to the boy?
He is missing. Look, it says so.
The public register says MISSING, in a clean hand.
The body is a separate matter. They took that out of a chamber room on the third floor.
Recovery entered on the internal sheet. External register to retain MISSING. Medical finding: not attached.
And the others knew. They are musicians. You cannot hide a missing boy from people who can hear which floor he is not on.
A notice went up. It is the one clear thing anybody there ever wrote down.
Acknowledge that his body was recovered here. Until that acknowledgment is made, we will not rehearse or perform. We will not play over what happened.
RECEIVED BY THE OFFICE. NO REPLY FILED.

choices.text: "What does that leave me to hear?"

lines.text: Good for them.
Is it not? Every room in the place silent, for the first time since it opened. You have no idea how lovely that was.
What did the school say?
They are still not answering. It is the longest piece anyone has ever performed there.
So nobody played. Some stopped eating. And some went up the tower, to the ringing room, where it is quiet.
Transfer receipts. Students' bodies, removed from the ringing room. The names checked against the register.
Cause of death: not entered on this copy. Rehearsal status: suspended.
"Refusal to rehearse is not a medical finding." Somebody sat down and typed that.
Did you do that?
Look at me. I am a hole. I have never so much as lifted a bow.
That isn't a no.
No, it is not. They told me you were cheap. They did not say you were quick.
Why are you telling me?
Because by midnight you will be standing in those rooms, being paid to hear nothing. Somebody ought to tell you what you will be hearing nothing of.
You say nothing. You have a professional reason.
That is it. That is exactly what they all did. You will fit right in.
The school tips. Your hands have corrected for a bend you cannot see.
Good. You are still driving.
Do you want me to put the next bit back where it was?
What next bit?
The bit where you decide to go in. People are very particular about the order.
Leave the road alone.
I have not touched it. You brought the bend with you.
Nothing in the picture straightens. You keep your hands where the road would need them.
You keep the small correction in your hands.
I will put you down as still driving. That gives us something to start from.
Now. You. I have been looking forward to you.
More of the eyes have turned this way than you would have thought it had left.
I have seen this night a good many ways. They are all very well made. Ask me one.

choices.text: "I'll finish the job and go home."
"I could get the last one out."
"Is there one where I'm all right?"

lines.text: Another?
I'll finish the job and go home.
You might! A car park. Morning. Nothing wrong with the light at all. A cup of coffee the guard gave you, gone cold.
You might listen back. Five clean minutes. Perhaps there is something on them. Perhaps you have just learned to hear it.
A perfectly ordinary morning. I would hate to be the one who made you doubt it.
Then I stop whatever this is.
You might. Suppose it closes. Suppose it works, even. People do like a job that stays done.
You would be on the inside, mind. Your own torch would be the last thing to go out.
Somebody will help me.
Somebody will. There is a man on the gate, and he is kind, and I am not being funny. He tries. They file it under what he tried.
It is the same ending, with a witness.
There's always another way out.
There is! It is not on the drawings. It is grey, and it opens, and you are so pleased.
I will not spoil what is behind it. There is a great deal more of it than you would think, and then another grey door.
I could get the last one out.
You would, too. Down the service road, into the morning, the two of you.
He will thank you. Do listen to who is doing the thanking.
I could just stop, and listen.
There is a bench. I would like that. There is a piece I want you to hear.
You sit. It holds your weight. There is no waking up farther along the corridor, and you will not mind as much as you should.
Is there one where I'm all right?
All of the eyes that are left look at you.
Who knows? Nothing is ever for certain.
You could always just drive off. People have. They never write.
That's enough.
It is. You have a bend coming up.
Last thing. In there, with the red light on and the needle at nothing: hold your breath.
You will want the practice.
All the eyes shut. The hole still seems to be looking.
When it gets quiet, do not hurry to be the next thing in it.
The wipers come back across.
You are nearly there. You have been nearly there for some time.
Your thumb is still on the seam. You do not remember checking which side of it.
